tool: validated HIP HBM-stream and empty-kernel launch microbenchmarks
purpose: Measure sustained device-memory bandwidth and host-to-device launch/materialization floors on the target runtime
capability_probe: HBM benchmark validates bytes read/written analytically and reports device events
launch benchmark reports empty-kernel batch slope after subtracting synchronization and timer overhead
both benchmarks record GPU clocks, runtime version, visible device and repetition variance
preconditions: use allocations substantially larger than cache for the HBM ceiling
report copy and read-modify-write byte conventions separately
fit launch batch time versus dispatch count instead of timing one synchronized launch
repeat per visible device and retain rank/device variance
cross-check HBM traffic with supported hardware counters when available

outputs.information: bytes, duration, bandwidth convention, size and variance
batch size, enqueue/device/synchronization timing and fitted launch slope
benchmark revision, command, runtime, clocks, scope, repetitions and raw paths

helps_diagnose: whether launch count can explain an observed floor

provenance.notes: No benchmark is marked ready until analytical byte and batched-launch tests are checked in; vendor theoretical peaks are sources, not measured ceilings.
